note: ADR-0011 §3.2, §3.3 and §3.5. Our own generic circuit values (varimu.h), held to the class of circuit, not to a product. The static gain is held to the three-halves law of the remote-cutoff cell, (1-u)^1.5, with 2 dB at the threshold, up to 12 dB of reduction (beyond it the peak detector's ripple moves the level the law is evaluated at faster than any bar is meaningful); the soft knee to a ratio rising with level; releases to the network's exponential through the cell's law at 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz; program positions to a release that lengthens after a long compression and to a fixed one that does not; attack to a multiple of tau (the rectifier charges on the peaks only). Aliasing of the gain cell per quality at 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz, 10 and 12 kHz tones at -18 dBFS. The standard and high bars are ADR-0011 §3.2's -90 dBc. Their detector runs at the oversampled rate (the key is up-sampled by the signal's own filter): rectified at 44.1 kHz, the sampled peaks of a 10 kHz tone beat against the rate (4f folds into the control band) and standard measured -89.1 dBc; at the oversampled rate it measures -106.9 (10 kHz) and -90.8 (12 kHz, the oversampler's stopband edge). The default quality is eco (no latency, the only quality held to the CPU class): standard costs about 61 us p99.9 on a 51.4 us calibrated bar, so it is offered, reported and not held, until optimised.
